subject.title: Version committed server-side after client 120s timeout is stuck hidden (versions:0, updatedAt frozen ~29h) — @borglife/plugin@0.2.1-beta.1

question: For the affected hidden version, should the publish/scan owner requeue its existing processing job, repair the persisted release state, or remove it so the publisher can create a clean replacement?
rationale: The observable symptoms establish a stuck release, but selecting a safe recovery action requires inspecting the actual stored release and scanner-job state rather than inferring it from the client timeline.

options.title: Inspect and recover the existing release
options.body: Recommended: inspect the package-version and scanner-job records, then requeue or repair the existing version only if its uploaded artifact and scan state are valid.

options.title: Invalidate the stranded version
options.body: Remove or mark the incomplete release invalid only if operator inspection shows no safe artifact or processing record can be recovered, allowing the publisher to upload a new version.

recommendation.title: Inspect and recover the existing release
recommendation.body: Recommended: inspect the package-version and scanner-job records, then requeue or repair the existing version only if its uploaded artifact and scan state are valid.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged publish-timeout work is the strongest available history signal for routing the initial inspection, while the dedicated scanner-state owner is not identifiable from the supplied evidence.
